description: Stage 0 of the jabberwock's OWN curriculum (docs/jabberwock_game_play_design.md): 'I can predict a passive world.' The forward model + the surprise signal — the predictor everything else is built on. Per its design: predict each Region's next CENTROID (not pixels — wrong altitude) from the constant-velocity prior (object_permanence + Newton's first law as a DEFAULT prediction): predicted.cy(t+1)=cy+drow, predicted.cx(t+1)=cx+dcol. The prediction is written in-fixpoint as next_predicted_* and COMMITTED at the clock edge by the engine's conservative fold (region carries clocked=1) — the only place the standing prediction can change. Surprise = |observed centroid − the prediction committed last tick|, per Region. Success (the agent's own criterion): per-Region one-step error → floor on a moving dot. No control, no goals, no death yet — only prediction.

microtheory.name: stage0_prediction
microtheory.description: predict each region's next centroid (constant velocity); surprise = observed - predicted; the predictor everything builds on.

rules.name: region_predict_next
rules.comment: The forward model (a graph Term): predict each Region's next centroid = current centroid + its tracked velocity (drow/dcol) — the constant-velocity prior (object_permanence). Written as next_predicted_* (combinational, in-fixpoint); the engine's clock-edge fold commits next_predicted_*→predicted_* (region carries clocked=1), so the standing prediction only changes at the clock edge.

rules.name: region_surprise
rules.comment: Surprise = the prediction error, per Region: |observed centroid − the centroid this Region was predicted (last tick, committed at the clock edge) to have now|. This single residual is the agent's currency (later it drives model update, attention, action; here it just measures whether the predictor works). predicted_cy/predicted_cx default to 0 before the first committed prediction (a one-off opening surprise).
